transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm here because of my eating. What really made me make the appointment is that... once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some kind of switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is in the background thinking, 'Dennis, just stop already.' I just can't seem to stop myself once it starts.
Do you usually feel guilty after one of these eating episodes?

Yeah, I do. Afterward, I just feel... embarrassed, honestly, and kind of grossed out with myself. It really bothers me because I'm usually pretty disciplined with my college classes and my robotics projects. So when I eat like that, it just makes me feel like I'm completely not in control.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these eating episodes?
No, not really. Um, my weight has actually stayed pretty much the same. I haven't noticed any big changes up or down, even with all the eating.
How often do these eating episodes happen?

Well, since early in the semester, it's been happening most weeks. Usually, it's just one night a week, but sometimes it's two if I have a lot of project deadlines or if food just kind of piles up in the apartment. I'd say it's been a pretty steady pattern for at least the last three or four months now.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after one of these eating episodes?
No, I've never done that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. I just... I just kind of sit with how bad I feel afterwards, I guess. But no, I don't do any of that.
Do you typically try to restrict your food intake between these eating episodes?
No, not really. I mean, I just eat normally on the other days. I'll go to the dining hall or grab whatever like I usually do. I don't try to, like, skip meals or go on a diet between those nights.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period under similar circumstances?

Yeah, I do. Like... on nights after a project deadline, or if there's just leftover pizza around the apartment, I can end up eating a lot. I'll eat a whole small pizza, plus chips, and then some cereal in my room. It's way more than I ever planned to eat, and definitely a lot more than what my roommates would eat for a normal dinner.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake on the days following one of these eating episodes?

No, I don't do that. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I just eat normally the next day. I don't ever fast or try to starve myself to make up for it or anything like that. I just... I just go to the dining hall and eat my regular meals.
Do you feel like you have no control over what or how much you're eating during those episodes?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, that is what really made me come in here. Once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already. But I just can't seem to stop in the moment.
Have these eating episodes caused any problems for you at college, with friends, or in other parts of your life?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm still making it to class and going to my robotics club meetings and everything. It hasn't actually knocked me off track or caused any major issues like that. But, um, I do sometimes feel a bit distracted or sluggish the next morning. And I definitely spend extra time worrying about whether my roommates noticed how much I ate. So... it bothers me a lot personally, but it hasn't really caused problems with my friends or schoolwork.
Do you feel guilty specifically because you feel like you've lost control during these eating episodes?

Yeah, exactly. Afterward, I just feel... embarrassed. And kind of grossed out with myself, honestly. I'm usually pretty disciplined when it comes to school and robotics, so... having these moments where I completely lose control, it really bothers me. It makes me feel like I'm just not in control of myself at all, which is definitely where a lot of that guilt comes from.
Do these episodes of eating, where you feel like you've lost control, occur at least once a week for the past three months?

Yeah, I'd say so. Since early in the semester, it's been happening most weeks. Usually just one night, but sometimes two if I have a lot of deadlines or if there's just a bunch of food sitting around the apartment. It's been pretty steady like that for at least the last three or four months.
Do you find that you're eating very quickly during these episodes?

Yeah, I do. During those times, I eat really fast. A lot of the time I'll just be standing at my desk, maybe in between doing homework and playing a game, and I'll just scarf it down. I barely even taste it, honestly. Then I'll look down a few minutes later and realize the whole thing is just... gone.
Have you avoided social situations because of your eating habits?

No, I don't think so. I still go out and hang out with my friends and everything. The eating mostly just happens when I'm already alone in my room late at night, so it hasn't really made me cancel plans or avoid seeing people.
Do you feel like these eating episodes are affecting your self-esteem or how you think about yourself as a person?

Yeah, they definitely do. I mean, right afterward, I just feel really embarrassed... and kind of grossed out with myself, honestly. It bothers me a lot because I'm usually pretty disciplined with things like my classes and the robotics team I'm on. I like to stay on top of my stuff. So when I eat like that, it just makes me feel like I'm completely not in control, and that definitely messes with how I see myself.
Do you usually feel uncomfortably full after one of these eating episodes?

Yeah, I do. I usually only stop eating when my stomach starts feeling really tight and heavy. It gets to the point where I just need to go lie down on my bed for a while because it's actually uncomfortable to stay sitting up at my desk.
